control_gap: Production mode does not fail closed when required boundary credentials are missing.

evidence.observation: Empty keys disable authentication and admin checks can fall back to normal auth.
Keys are dashboard-supplied but no startup assertion is declared.

impact: Unauthenticated callers can consume model/storage resources and, when both controls are absent, administer the knowledge base.
remediation_seed: Define production mode that refuses startup unless separate API/admin credentials or stronger identity-aware authorization are configured and rotated.
reproducibility: Start an isolated configuration with empty synthetic keys and inspect guard outcomes; do not bind a live server.
root_cause: Authentication keys are optional, empty values disable checks, document administration falls back to normal authentication, and deployment configuration does not enforce non-empty values at startup.

security_privacy_details.actor_or_failure_source: Unauthenticated internet client or deployment misconfiguration
security_privacy_details.asset: Model quota, conversations, metrics, document administration
security_privacy_details.sensitive_data_impact: Unauthorized creation/access paths and possible knowledge poisoning

title: Production can start with API and admin authentication disabled
trigger_conditions: Service is reachable by untrusted clients

control_gap: No pre-identity network/credential bucket or durable abuse signal constrains identity creation.

evidence.observation: Rate-limit identity is derived from the request principal.
A missing token causes a new random principal to be issued.
Buckets are keyed only by the provided key.

existing_controls: Optional API authentication can provide a stable credential when enabled
impact: Automated clients can multiply request allowance, increasing denial-of-wallet, abuse, and availability risk.
remediation_seed: Layer limits by trusted API principal and coarse network/device signals before identity issuance, with privacy-preserving distributed enforcement.
reproducibility: Call request-boundary helpers with repeated synthetic requests that retain no identity and compare generated keys/buckets.
root_cause: A request without a valid identity is issued a fresh pseudonymous user ID before rate-limit keying, so clients that discard cookies or headers can obtain new buckets.

security_privacy_details.sensitive_data_impact: Indirect; abuse can degrade service for vulnerable users

title: Anonymous identity churn can evade rate limits
trigger_conditions: Caller omits/discards identity cookie and header between requests

control_gap: Global cleanup does not evaluate timestamp age for idle non-empty buckets.

evidence.observation: Only the active bucket is expired; threshold cleanup tests whether other deques are empty without aging them.

existing_controls: Per-bucket timestamps use a bounded one-minute window
impact: Long-running workers can accumulate unbounded key dictionaries and waste memory under accidental or malicious identity churn.
remediation_seed: Age all sampled buckets, cap key cardinality, and use a bounded/distributed limiter with explicit eviction metrics.
reproducibility: Use a synthetic clock or aged deques in an isolated unit harness and trigger cleanup from a different key.
root_cause: Expired timestamps are removed only from the bucket being checked; global cleanup removes only already-empty buckets, so one-time identities remain non-empty forever unless revisited.
title: Rate-limiter cleanup cannot remove stale non-empty buckets
trigger_conditions: More than 10,000 unique identities each make one request and never return

control_gap: No server-enforced token lifetime, rotation key ID, session revocation list, or reauthentication mechanism exists.

evidence.observation: Payload contains only version, user ID, and session ID.
Verification checks signature/version/ID shape but not time or revocation.
Cookie age is client transport metadata, not token expiry.

existing_controls: Account tombstones can block known users
impact: A stolen bearer-like identity can remain valid for years or beyond user-side cookie deletion, enabling continued access to owner-scoped records.
remediation_seed: Add bounded token lifetimes, rotation key identifiers, revocation/session epochs, and secure re-issuance with migration support.
reproducibility: Issue a synthetic token, advance an isolated clock beyond cookie age, and verify that token parsing has no time check.
root_cause: Identity payloads contain version and IDs but no issued-at, expiry, key identifier, or revocation epoch; header tokens are not constrained by cookie max-age.

security_privacy_details.sensitive_data_impact: Long-lived unauthorized access to personal and health-related records
security_privacy_details.trust_boundary: Client-provided identity header/cookie to server principal

title: Signed identity tokens have no intrinsic expiry or revocation
trigger_conditions: A token is copied or stolen
Token is replayed through the identity header

control_gap: Runtime authorization does not protect repository history, and ordinary deletion cannot purge existing clones.

evidence.observation: The application database path is tracked; content was not opened.
Version-control metadata confirms persistence risk without reproducing values.

existing_controls: No database values were read or reproduced during audit
Application owner checks protect runtime queries
impact: Current or historical sensitive records may be distributed through repository clones and remain recoverable after working-tree deletion.
remediation_seed: Immediately restrict repository access and stop tracking runtime data; assess exposure, purge history safely, rotate affected secrets/identifiers, notify as required, and verify all clones/backups.
reproducibility: Run read-only Git tracked-file metadata inspection; do not open the database or print content.
root_cause: Git metadata identifies data/chat_archive.sqlite3 as tracked, placing a persistent application database within version-controlled repository history.

security_privacy_details.actor_or_failure_source: Repository reader, clone recipient, or history compromise
security_privacy_details.sensitive_data_impact: Potential conversation and inferred health-data exposure; values intentionally not inspected
security_privacy_details.trust_boundary: Runtime data directory to version-control distribution

title: A conversation archive database is tracked in Git
trigger_conditions: The tracked database contains or previously contained user conversations or derived state
Repository clones, backups, or history are accessible

control_gap: No application or repository-declared platform header baseline exists.

evidence.observation: No explicit security-header response hook is defined.

existing_controls: UI inserts chat text with textContent
external_validation_needed: Production edge/TLS header injection requires deployment validation.
impact: Defense in depth against framing, mixed transport, content injection, and referrer leakage is reduced.
non_reproducibility_reason: The live edge was not contacted; missing repository evidence supports a future risk.
remediation_seed: Define and test an application/platform security-header baseline with CSP nonces/hashes and staged compatibility review.
reproducibility: Static review only; platform-injected headers require external validation.
root_cause: Flask responses and deployment configuration contain no repository-evident Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, frame-ancestor/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or related response-header policy.

security_privacy_details.actor_or_failure_source: Web attacker exploiting future browser-content or framing weakness
security_privacy_details.sensitive_data_impact: Potential UI/session exposure if another defect is exploitable

title: Browser security headers are not explicitly enforced
trigger_conditions: The browser UI is publicly deployed
A future template/script injection or framing attack is possible
TLS termination does not inject equivalent headers

control_gap: There is no repository-evident consent/notice, data classification filter, minimum-necessary selection, or provider-side retention assurance.

evidence.observation: Multiple user-context sources are combined for model input.
Safety reasoning can send bounded transcript content to a model.
Provider APIs are the external processing boundary.

external_validation_needed: Provider retention, training, region, and contractual controls require external validation.
impact: Sensitive user data crosses an external trust boundary with scope and downstream retention not controlled by repository logic.
remediation_seed: Establish explicit notice/consent, data minimization and redaction, provider no-retention controls, regional/legal review, and auditable transmission metadata without content logging.
reproducibility: Static trace only; no external provider call or user data inspection was performed.
root_cause: Current messages, recent transcripts, summaries, memories, inferred health state, and knowledge can be assembled for provider calls; no consent, per-field minimization, provider retention configuration, or data-processing policy is enforced in code/config.
